S1: Task planned on 2026-11-21 from the owner's request and the ChatGPT Pro audit of the same day (GitHub as the final boundary). Filed by S21 on the owner's written instruction in https://claude.ai/code/session_016Q3DcWsMTSxPxJa7tMeDAs; the owner may amend or close it.

**Slot:** `slot:S10`. **Audit section:** 6; P1 row 9.

### Goal
An agent can do only what its capability set names, in `<domain>.<action>` form across the product, not only code: `research.read`, `research.write`, `company.read`, `company.write`, `fund.read`, `relationships.read`, `relationships.request-introduction`, `code.read`, `code.branch`, `code.commit`, `code.pr`, `deploy.preview`, `deploy.staging`, `cloud.read`, `finance.read`, `legal.read`, `legal.draft`, `email.read`, `email.draft`, `web.search`. `code.merge`, `deploy.production`, `cloud.write`, `finance.execute` and `email.send` exist as names and are never grantable to an agent (a person does them). The Worker refuses the rest with a code, and the HQ screen shows the matrix. A founder can then deploy a Market Research Agent with `research.*`, `company.read`, `fund.read`, `web.search` and nothing else.

### Scope
- Migration `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<issue>_agent_capabilities.sql`: `agent_capabilities` (agent_id, capability, granted_by, granted_at, revoked_at), a `capability_catalog` seeded with the names above (domain, action, grantable 0/1, one sentence), and the platform ceiling on `ai_agent_policy` (which grantable capabilities the platform offers this month).
- `cloudflare-worker/src/services/agentCapabilities.ts`: `requireCapability(agent, name)` → ok or refusal `capability_missing` (`capability_ungrantable` for the five reserved names); wire it into the publish request path (#5569's `agent_publish_requests`: `code.pr`), the run admission (`agent_engine.ts`: the task's module maps to a domain action), the compute job dispatch (`agent_compute.ts`: `cloud.read`), the preview deploy trigger (`deploy.preview`), and the skills runner's tool calls (`team_skills.ts`: the tool's declared capability). Wildcards (`research.*`) expand at grant time into rows, never at check time. Bump `agent_authz_revisions` on every grant or revoke (#5567's pattern).
- Routes under `admin_ai_agents_policy.ts`: read the matrix, grant, revoke; super admin only; every write audited.
- Frontend: HQ › AI agents › Operations › Policies gets the matrix (boards SA10 to SA14 below, once the canvas lands); until then build everything that does not depend on layout.

### Files owned
The migration, `cloudflare-worker/src/services/agentCapabilities.ts` (new), the four call sites named (one guarded call each), `cloudflare-worker/src/routes/admin_ai_agents_policy.ts`, `cloudflare-worker/test/agent_capabilities_<issue>.test.ts`, `frontend/src/pages/hq/aiAgents/CapabilityMatrix.jsx` (new) and its test, `frontend/src/lib/api/aiAgentsPolicy.js` (new methods), `documentation/architecture/decisions/D<issue>.md`.

### Decision and migration numbers
D<this issue>; migration `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<issue>_agent_capabilities.sql` (UTC minute when written).

### Dependencies
Tracker: #8059.
Builds on D1528 (engine), #5567 (authz revisions), #5569 (publisher). The screen waits on the canvas (needs-design, prompt below); the Worker and the data do not.

### Done when
A green draft PR carrying D<issue>: refusals tested at all four call sites, the five reserved names ungrantable by test, the matrix routes audited, and the screen built to the approved canvas (or the PR says the screen is deferred to a second PR on this issue).

### Design prompt (Missing UI; AGENTS.md)

**Continues:** `HQ AI Agents` (`design/incoming/HQ AI Agents Page.dc.html`), boards from **SA10**. Decision file: `D4137-p<k>.md` for the addendum.
**Shared rules it uses:** Platform States (ST-00 to ST-14, D5129) · the Eadwyn rail (#5130) · `design/tokens/tokens.json`.

**What the platform records** (checked on main `270cdf4a2a`):

| Value on screen | Read from | Stored in | Can be missing | Can fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agent name, role, status | `GET /api/admin/ai-agents/roster` | `team_agents` | no | yes |
| ◇ Capability granted / revoked, by whom, when | ◇ `GET /api/admin/ai-agents/policy/capabilities` | ◇ `agent_capabilities` | yes | yes |
| ◇ Platform ceiling per capability | ◇ same | ◇ `ai_agent_policy` | yes | yes |
| Last refusal (code, when) | `GET /api/agent-engine/runs/:uid` | `agent_task_runs.refusal` | yes | yes |

Backend required (drawn with ◇, not built): the two routes and the table above, this issue.

```text
You are designing new boards for Axal VC / StudioOS, continuing the canvas "HQ AI Agents".
Keep its frame, components, type and colours. Number the new boards SA10 onward.

SURFACE
- Route: /hq/ai-agents/operations/policies. Who sees it: super admin. Reached from: HQ › AI agents › Operations › Policies tab.
- The job: see at a glance what each agent may do, grant or revoke one capability with a reason, and understand why a run was refused.

WHAT IS RECORDED (draw only these; ◇ marks a value that needs backend work)
- Agent: name, role, status (live, paused, retired).
- ◇ Capability per agent, grouped by domain (research, company, fund, relationships, code, deploy, cloud, finance, legal, email, web): granted (by whom, when) or not; code.merge, deploy.production, cloud.write, finance.execute and email.send are shown as locked rows that no one can grant.
- ◇ Platform ceiling: which capabilities the platform offers at all this month.
- Last refusal: code and time of the agent's most recent refused run, if any.

BOARDS
SA10 · Capability matrix · desktop 1440
  Shows: agents as rows, capabilities as columns grouped by domain with a collapse per domain, a cell is granted (word + check), not granted, or locked (the five reserved names). Filter by role and status. Primary action: grant or revoke in a side panel with a required reason (≤ 200 characters). Eadwyn: proposes revoking a capability unused for 30 days; accept, edit or discard.
SA11 · Grant panel · desktop 1440
  The side panel open on one cell: agent, capability, what it allows in one sentence, who granted it last, the reason field, Grant / Revoke. A refusal from the Worker is shown inline with its code.
SA12 · States · desktop 1440
  Loading · Not recorded (no capability granted yet: every cell empty with the one action) · Unreadable (the roster read failed; the ceiling row still works; Try again) · Refused (not a super admin: who can grant access) · Saving and save failed (the panel keeps its text).
SA13 · Phone 390
  Agents as cards, each listing its granted capabilities as chips; tap a card for the panel as a sheet; 44px targets.
SA14 · Dark · desktop 1440
  SA10 on the dark tokens; states keep their words and shapes.

RULES
- Every figure says what it counts and for which period. Zero, Not recorded and Unreadable never look alike.
- Colour never carries meaning alone: a word or a glyph goes with it.
- Sample content only: bracketed names and figures.
- Handoff: a cell's "last refusal" opens the run in HQ › AI agents › Operations › Audit, carrying the run id.

QUESTIONS FOR THE OWNER (draw option A unless told otherwise)
- Is the matrix per agent or per role with per-agent exceptions? A) per agent, with a "apply to role" action B) per role only. Pick: A.
- Should a revoke take effect on live runs? A) at the next run; live runs finish B) halts live runs. Pick: A.
```

**Next:** the owner runs this in Claude Design and links the canvas here. On approval, S1 lands it with `land-canvas` and removes `needs-design`.

**Slot:** `slot:S11`. **Audit section:** 7; P1 row 10.

### Goal
An agent cannot spend past what its sponsor set: a per-agent monthly budget (tokens and minutes), a per-task ceiling (tokens, minutes, retries) and a per-agent daily PR count. A workspace (company or project) also has ceilings: agents in total, agents live at once, AI spend per month, compute spend per month, production deploys per day (0 for agents, by the capability task of this epic). Exhaustion halts the run with a refusal code the HQ screen shows; nothing is silently truncated.

### Scope
- Migration `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<issue>_agent_budgets.sql`: `agent_budgets` (agent_id, period, tokens_cap, minutes_cap, prs_per_day_cap, retries_per_task_cap, set_by, set_at) and `agent_budget_usage` (agent_id, period_key, tokens_used, minutes_used, prs_opened) kept by the workflow; task-level caps as nullable columns on `scope_tasks` (NULL = the agent's cap); workspace ceilings as columns on `agent_scope_settings` (agents_cap, live_agents_cap, ai_spend_cap_cents, compute_spend_cap_cents; NULL = the platform's figure on `ai_agent_policy`). Compute spend reads `agent_compute_jobs` (cpu_ms, wall_ms) priced by the rate card the decision file records.
- `cloudflare-worker/src/services/agentBudgets.ts`: `reserve(run, estimate)` before each model call and before a publish, `settle(run, actual)` after; on exhaustion the workflow moves the run to `halted` with refusal `budget_exhausted` and posts the step summary (D1528's `steps_json`). Reuse the usage ledger the gateway already writes (#7073); do not create a second ledger.
- Routes under `admin_ai_agents_policy.ts` to read and set budgets (super admin), and a read for the sponsor in `team_agents.ts`.
- Frontend: HQ › AI agents › Operations › Spend gets the budget panel (boards SA15 to SA19); build the rest first.

### Files owned
The migration, `cloudflare-worker/src/services/agentBudgets.ts` (new), the reserve/settle calls in the `AgentTaskWorkflow` step runner (one call each), `cloudflare-worker/src/routes/admin_ai_agents_policy.ts` (budget routes), `cloudflare-worker/src/routes/team_agents.ts` (one read), `cloudflare-worker/test/agent_budgets_<issue>.test.ts`, `frontend/src/pages/hq/aiAgents/BudgetPanel.jsx` (new) and its test, `documentation/architecture/decisions/D<issue>.md`.

### Decision and migration numbers
D<this issue>; migration `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<issue>_agent_budgets.sql`.

### Dependencies
Tracker: #8059.
After #7074 (capacity, lanes) is on main; reads #7072's owner answers (S21). Hierarchy (#8081) bounds children by the parent's budget through this service. Screen waits on the canvas below.

### Done when
A green draft PR carrying D<issue>: a run that would exceed any cap halts with `budget_exhausted` in tests, usage settles exactly once per step, the routes are audited, and the panel is built to the approved canvas or deferred explicitly.

### Design prompt (Missing UI; AGENTS.md)

**Continues:** `HQ AI Agents` (`design/incoming/HQ AI Agents Page.dc.html`), boards from **SA15**. Decision file: `D4137-p<k>.md` for the addendum.
**Shared rules it uses:** Platform States (ST-00 to ST-14, D5129) · the Eadwyn rail (#5130) · `design/tokens/tokens.json`.

**What the platform records** (checked on main `270cdf4a2a`):

| Value on screen | Read from | Stored in | Can be missing | Can fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tokens and cost this month, per agent | `GET /api/admin/ai-agents/operations/spend` | the AI usage ledger (D1528 / #7073) | yes | yes |
| ◇ Caps: tokens, minutes, PRs per day, retries per task | ◇ `GET /api/admin/ai-agents/policy/budgets` | ◇ `agent_budgets` | yes | yes |
| ◇ Used against each cap, this period | ◇ same | ◇ `agent_budget_usage` | yes | yes |
| Runs halted for budget (code, when) | `GET /api/agent-engine/agents/:uid/runs` | `agent_task_runs.refusal = budget_exhausted` | yes | yes |

Backend required (drawn with ◇, not built): the routes and tables above, this issue.

```text
You are designing new boards for Axal VC / StudioOS, continuing the canvas "HQ AI Agents".
Keep its frame, components, type and colours. Number the new boards SA15 onward.

SURFACE
- Route: /hq/ai-agents/operations/spend. Who sees it: super admin; a sponsor sees their own agents' panel read-only in Team. Reached from: HQ › AI agents › Operations › Spend.
- The job: see how much of each budget an agent has used this period, raise or lower a cap with a reason, and see which runs were halted for budget.

WHAT IS RECORDED (draw only these; ◇ marks a value that needs backend work)
- Spend this month per agent: tokens and cost, from the usage ledger.
- ◇ Caps per agent: tokens per month, minutes per month, PRs per day, retries per task; who set each and when.
- ◇ Workspace ceilings: agents in total, live at once, AI spend and compute spend per month, as used / cap, above the agent table.
- ◇ Used against each cap this period, as a figure and a share.
- Halted runs: time, task, refusal code budget_exhausted.

BOARDS
SA15 · Budgets · desktop 1440
  Shows: per agent, four meters (tokens, minutes, PRs today, retries) each labelled with used / cap and the period; a sort by share used; the halted-runs list under the table. Primary action: edit caps in a side panel with a reason. Eadwyn: proposes a cap from the last three months' usage; accept, edit or discard.

SA18 · Phone 390
  One agent per card with the four meters stacked; tap for the panel as a sheet; 44px targets.
SA19 · Dark · desktop 1440
  SA15 on the dark tokens; states keep their words and shapes.

RULES
- Every figure says what it counts and for which period. Zero, Not recorded and Unreadable never look alike.
- Colour never carries meaning alone: a word or a glyph goes with it.
- Sample content only: bracketed names and figures.
- Handoff: a halted run opens in Operations › Audit with the run id; "Spend" figures link to the AI usage page for the agent.

QUESTIONS FOR THE OWNER (draw option A unless told otherwise)
- Budget period: A) calendar month, UTC B) rolling 30 days. Pick: A.
- Who may raise a cap above the platform ceiling? A) nobody; the ceiling is edited on Policies B) super admin inline. Pick: A.
```

### Goal
A job that runs code from a pull request can never reach a credential: it runs in the `untrusted` runner group (or hosted), with `permissions: contents: read` and nothing else, no `secrets.*` and no `id-token`. Privileged work (deploys, publishes) runs only in `trusted` from `main`.

### Scope
- `scripts/ci/pool-contract.mjs`: parse every workflow; for each job triggered by `pull_request` or `merge_group`, assert the contract above; for each job that names a deploy environment, assert `runs-on` names the trusted group (or a hosted label) and the trigger is `push` to `main` or `workflow_dispatch`. Output a table; exit non-zero on a violation.
- `frontend/test/pool_contract_<issue>.test.mjs` runs it over the tree and over fixtures (one good, one of each violation).
- Fix the CI workflows that violate it today (`ci.yml`, the landing workflows' PR-triggered jobs, scan workflows): job-level `permissions:`, remove unneeded `secrets.` reads. If a job genuinely needs a secret on a PR (say which), the decision file records it as an exception with an expiry and the test allows it by name.
- Out of scope: deploy and ops workflows (#8069), the runner groups themselves (#8065), the executor and coordinator (#7886, #7887, #7909).

### Files owned
`scripts/ci/pool-contract.mjs` (new), `frontend/test/pool_contract_<issue>.test.mjs` (new), the PR-triggered CI workflows' `permissions:` and `runs-on` lines only (`ci.yml`, `codeql*.yml`, `semgrep*.yml`, `dependency-review*.yml`, `landing-policy.yml`), `documentation/architecture/decisions/D<issue>.md`.
